eli5.text: In the CLI chat, if the chat window's content height shifts suddenly without a scroll action, the UI now re-renders the scrollbox to keep the display in sync. ai.summary: Split monolithic `message-block.tsx` into dedicated components for agent lists, markdown content, thinking blocks, tool branches, and plan boxes. This modularization isolates rendering logic for specific content types, improving maintainability and testability within the CLI interface.

eli5.text: The command-line assistant used to draw every kind of message, lists of helper agents, formatted text, thinking notes, tool actions, and step-by-step plans, all from one giant, tangled block of code. Now those different pieces are each handled by their own dedicated drawing routine, so the code is easier to read and fix. You wouldn't notice a change in what appears on your screen today, but the display logic behind the scenes is cleaner and less likely to break going forward.

ai.title: CLI pause queue and cleaner status bar
ai.summary: Refactors CLI status handling into `StatusBar` and `ScrollToBottomButton`, removing `StatusIndicator`. Adds pause queue controls via `useQueueControls` and `useQueueUi`. Improves `MultilineInput` cursor handling for tabs and control chars. Scope: `cli/src/components`, `cli/src/hooks`, `cli/src/chat.tsx`.

eli5.text: The status area at the bottom of the CLI chat has been completely redesigned into a single, cleaner bar. Previously, the status indicator showed text like the assistant's current state and elapsed time, but it was a separate component; now it is consolidated into a new StatusBar that also includes a scroll-to-bottom button that appears only when you have scrolled up away from the latest message. The developers also added a pause queue feature, allowing you to temporarily stop and resume the incoming message stream, which is especially useful if you need to catch up on text that is scrolling by too quickly. Additionally, the text input area's cursor now correctly handles tabs and control characters, preventing it from jumping to incorrect positions when editing your prompt.

ai.title: SDK adds spawn injection for git state
ai.summary: SDK introduces `CodebuffSpawn` type and `spawn`/`spawnSource` options to `run` and `InitialSessionStateOptions`. This enables injecting `child_process.spawn` to compute initial git status, diffs, and commit logs for session state. Changes affect `common/src/types/spawn.ts`, `sdk/src/run.ts`, and `sdk/src/run-state.ts`. Default behavior falls back to Node's `child_process.spawn` if `spawnSource` is omitted.

eli5.text: If you use Codebuff's assistant tooling to analyze a project that lives in a Git repository, the SDK can now run Git commands through a custom shell handler you provide instead of always using the built-in one. This matters when your environment restricts or redirects how shell commands execute, because the initial project snapshot (files, recent changes, and commit history) is now fetched via whatever command runner you specify. If you don't supply a custom handler, it falls back to the standard Node.js shell, so everyday behavior stays the same. The feature is in place and ready to use.

ai.title: AbortSignal threaded through agent runtime and SDK run
ai.summary: Added AbortSignal parameter to loopAgentSteps, processStreamWithTools, CodebuffToolHandlerFunction, ExecuteToolCallParams, and SDK run(). Checks signal.aborted before tool execution and in main loop, returning 'Run cancelled by user' error. WebSocket and evals pass new AbortController().signal.

eli5.text: If you or your integration cancels a run (for example, by stopping mid-response or timing out), the agent now stops immediately instead of continuing to call tools or send output. A cancellation signal travels through the same internal pathways used during normal runs, including the SDK's run() function, the core agent loop, and the real-time WebSocket connections, so the stop is respected consistently across the entire flow. When you cancel, you see a brief 'Run cancelled by user' error instead of partial tool calls or streamed output finishing.

ai.title: Catch all errors in SDK run
ai.summary: SDK `run` now catches all errors, returning `getCancelledRunState` with the error message instead of throwing. `getCancelledAdditionalMessages` accepts a `systemMessage` parameter to inject dynamic cancellation text. Invalid API keys return a structured error state rather than throwing. Covers `sdk/src/run.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/messages.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant's run is cancelled or the API key is invalid, the program used to crash by throwing an error; now it captures the failure and returns a clean "cancelled" state with the error message shown to you. You'll see the run stop gracefully with a readable reason instead of the program suddenly aborting, and the cancellation notice can now include custom dynamic text explaining why it stopped. It's live today across the SDK run path and the messaging utility.

ai.title: SDK version bumped to 0.9.1
ai.summary: The SDK package version increments from 0.9.0 to 0.9.1 as a release-bump commit affecting only sdk/package.json. This release bundles the features and changes documented in the 0.9.1 changelog entries, including spawn injection for git state, error catching in run, and the AGENTS.md knowledge file fallback, though the bump itself is a metadata-only change in this commit. The version bump aligns the published SDK with the accumulated work in the surrounding commit sequence.
ai.evidence: Commit ee4724ac bumps the version field in sdk/package.json from 0.9.0 to 0.9.1; no other files modified in this single-hunk, release-bump commit.

eli5.text: This release adds a new /usage command so you can check your remaining coding credits right from the terminal, and it upgrades the agent model that powers the fastest mode to be quicker and cheaper for simple tasks. It also introduces new built-in helpers that review your code in parallel and pick the best suggestion, plus a smarter way to search for files in your project using the @ key. The terminal interface now adapts its colors to match your app theme automatically, including better support for Visual Studio Code, Zed, and Windows PowerShell, and the chat display got a refreshed look with clearer mode indicators and a scroll-to-bottom button. Upgrading gives you a more responsive, visually consistent coding experience with finer control over costs and agent behavior, and it makes multi-step code reviews faster through parallel evaluation.
